descriptor: Fin-and-tube heat exchangers for HVAC, data centres and buses
lede: A Neemrana maker of copper-aluminium heat exchangers that built a plant six times its old size and is now filling it: Q1 FY27 revenue more than doubled on data-centre and export orders. The growth is real, but it has eaten cash, needed a ₹350 Cr equity raise within two years of the IPO, and the stock already prices in management's FY28 goal.

short_version.text: Revenue +40% in each of the last two years to ₹600 Cr in FY26, and Q1 FY27 +119% to ₹252 Cr at a 19.4% EBITDA margin. The new plant did ~₹115 Cr in its first full quarter, exports rose 177%, and Schneider, Vertiv and US data-centre customers are on board.

Operating cash flow was –₹114 Cr in FY26 with inventory at 242 days; the IPO money went into the plant and a ₹350 Cr QIP followed in June 2026. 95% of revenue is still one product (fin-and-tube), and the Bus AC and railway lines are early.
~99x trailing earnings and ~68x EV/EBITDA, against 26x for Subros and 73x for Inox India.

blocks.text: KRN makes fin-and-tube heat exchangers (coils), plus headers, copper parts and sheet-metal assemblies, for HVAC&R makers. Customers use them in commercial and room air-conditioners, chillers, data-centre cooling units, refrigerators and transport. A wholly owned subsidiary, KRN HVAC Products, runs the new plant, which adds bar-and-plate exchangers, refrigeration condensers and evaporators, dry coolers, oil coolers and complete Bus AC systems.

items.text: Customised, rolling orders (not projects); copper, aluminium and USD/INR passed through every quarter, with a one-quarter lag.
Exports earn better margins than domestic sales; PLI (5% on heat-exchanger output) and a 10-year Rajasthan incentive (RIPS) are still to be booked.
The subsidiary pays a concessional 15% tax rate.
IPO in October 2024; revenue from ₹307 Cr (FY24) to ₹600 Cr (FY26).
New plant started production in May 2025, fully commissioned in March 2026.
Bought the Bus AC business of Sphere Refrigeration Systems (Q2 FY26); approved by Indian Railways for bar-and-plate coolers.
₹350 Cr QIP in June 2026 (ADIA among investors).

items.text: borrowings ₹187 Cr at March 2026 (0.33x equity), interest cover ~17x; the June QIP should cut debt.
Capital employed rose ~₹544 Cr from FY24 to FY26 while post-tax operating profit rose ~₹32 Cr, because the new plant is still mostly empty. ROCE fell from 21% to 16%.
the parent sold ₹174 Cr to its own subsidiary in FY26 and lent it ₹102 Cr, so standalone growth (57%) overstates the business; use consolidated figures.

Foreign institutions rose to 8.9% from 2.4% a year ago; domestic institutions 8.3%.
Auditors made revenue recognition a key audit matter, citing fast growth, a new trading activity and the volume of related-party transactions.
Related-party purchases 37.5% and sales 25.8% of standalone totals, mostly with the KRN HVAC subsidiary.
MD's pay ₹90 lakh (24x median employee); ESOP plan approved in April 2026.
Answers on calls are often vague (segment data 'not prepared', QIP purpose 'not concluded').

blocks.text: There is no listed pure-play coil maker. Subros (auto and bus AC) and Amber (room-AC components) are the closest HVAC suppliers; Inox India and Harsha are export-heavy engineering peers. Many AC makers build coils in-house.

items.text: claims to be the largest independent heat-exchanger maker in India, with in-house sheet metal and tubing.

items.text: Management's goal is met: ~₹2,000 Cr revenue in FY28 at a 13% net margin (₹260 Cr), valued at 45x.

items.name: Base
items.text: Ramp is slower: ~₹1,500 Cr revenue at a 12% net margin (₹180 Cr), valued at 40x.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Plant stays half empty: ~₹1,100 Cr revenue at a 10% net margin (₹110 Cr), valued at 30x.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

KRN has the capacity, approvals and customers to grow several-fold, and Q1 FY27 shows the ramp has begun. But the price already assumes management's ~₹2,000 Cr FY28 goal; anything short of it, or another year of cash-hungry growth, would leave the stock looking expensive.
